catalog_locator: Abstract p.63; sec. 2.1 Taoping pp.64-65; sec. 2.3 Mianchi p.69; sec. 4.1-4.2 p.81
catalog_quote: [Abstract, p.63] In the Qiang language, the Southern dialects (SQ) exploit tones to make lexical distinctions, while the Northern dialects (NQ) lack tonal phenomena. ... Some dialects (Longxi, Taoping) have developed full-blown tonal systems, while others (Mianchi, Heihu) have layers of tonal strata over pitch accent systems. ... [2.1] Taoping has six tones (33, 55, 31, 241, 13, 51) ... Tones 33, 55, and 31 (the major tones) may all co-occur in any order ... [2.3, p.69] Tones in Mianchi ... are added onto a pitch accent system of high and low (-falling) pitch, in which native words may only have one high-pitched, or accented, syllable. ... in Mianchi a phonological word (usually mono- or disyllabic, although longer forms also occur) may be accented or unaccented, and the accent may occur on any syllable, although there are some restrictions; e.g., accented DIR prefixes only occur with v…

tone_statements.citation: Sims, Nathaniel A. 2025. Tonoexodus in Rma. Diachronica 42(2): 198-249. doi:10.1075/dia.22017.sim
tone_statements.quote: There are both tonal and atonal Rma dialects. It has been argued that tonal patterns emerged from reanalysis of stress patterns as tones due to influence from Chinese. This paper argues that the tonoexodus scenario explains word-prosodic correspondences better than the alternative tonogenetic account.
tone_statements.summary: SQ disyllabic tone patterns treated as inherited; NQ atonality as tone loss; explicitly engages the stress-vs-tone reanalysis question.

sources.quote: 'Four tones can be found in Longxi Qiang' (H 55, L 33~31, R 213, F 51; noun bí 'urine' vs verb bì 'urinate'). fn.1: 'Among recorded Qiang varieties, Mawo, Qugu, Ronghong, and Puxi are atonal; Taoping, Longxi, Mianchi, and Yonghe are tonal.' No word-stress rule stated; tone sandhi (dissimilation/assimilation) described.

sources.quote: Instrumental (8 speakers, LME) study of Luobuzhai, a tonal SQ-area village (Wenchuan): 'High (á) and Low (à) tones can distinguish lexical items ... Neither source mentions lexical or phrasal stress'; 'relative intensity (taken as a surrogate for stress) [was] not found to be significant. The status of lexical stress in this language is not yet fully understood'; 'no other prototypical reflections of stress were noticeably present (duration, intensity, vowel quality changes, etc.)'. Notes culminativity of H (Mianchi) is not observed in Luobuzhai.

sources.citation: Sims, Nathaniel A. 2020. Reconsidering the diachrony of tone in Rma. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 13(1): 53-85.http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52460
sources.quote: The subgroup-internal evidence comes from regular correspondences between tonal varieties. These data allow us to put forward a working hypothesis that proto-Rma had a two-way tonal contrast. Furthermore, existing accounts of how tonogenesis occurred in the tonal varieties are shown to be problematic.
sources.note: Prior work (Liu 1998, Evans 2001a-b) held that proto-Rma was non-tonal and the tonal varieties underwent tonogenesis; the paper re-examines those arguments, shows regular tone correspondences between the tonal varieties, proposes that proto-Rma had a two-way tonal contrast, argues the existing tonogenesis accounts are problematic, and adduces regular tonal correspondences with Prinmi and Tangut.
